models_evaluated: DB GPT (RAG on curated Q&A database, GPT-4)

links.outcome: Scientific consensus and error rates of RAG-grounded models versus ungrounded GPT-4o and electrophysiologist
links.effect: Scientific consensus: DB GPT 67%, PubMed GPT 62%, GPT-4o 88%, electrophysiologist 80%; PubMed GPT OR 0.35 (0.16–0.81). RAG models had similar error rates to physician; GPT-4o had lower incorrect retrieval and comprehension.
links.quote: However, the RAG models showed weaker performance than GPT-4o alone in areas requiring comprehensive understanding and reasoning.

links.outcome: Comparison of LLM responses against electrophysiologist responses on ten dimensions
links.effect: GPT-4o had lower error rates and higher specialized content (OR 10.80), empathy (OR 5.55), and helpfulness (OR 6.74) than the electrophysiologist; RAG models were comparable.
links.quote: For Evidence of Incorrect Comprehension, GPT-4o demonstrated a significantly lower error rate compared with the electrophysiologist (OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.40–8.30), whereas DB GPT and PubMed GPT showed comparable performance (OR 1.06 [0.49–2.29] and 0.64 [0.30–1.37], respectively).

links.outcome: Accuracy and safety of LLM lifestyle guidance versus expert-rated reference
links.effect: Scientific consensus 62–88% across LLMs; incorrect content 29% for DB GPT and PubMed GPT, 12.1% for GPT-4o; moderate or severe harm 24.2% DB GPT, 22% PubMed GPT, 9.1% GPT-4o.
links.quote: Scientific Consensus was observed in 80.0% of responses for the electrophysiologist, 67.0% for DB GPT, 62.0% for PubMed GPT, and 88.0% for GPT-4o.

openai.sample_unit: patient questions rated by five electrophysiologists (from 66 deduplicated questions)

links.effect: GPT-4o scientific consensus was 88.0% vs EP 80.0% and incorrect comprehension 15.0% vs 34.0% (OR 3.41 [1.40–8.30]); DB/PubMed consensus was 67.0%/62.0%.
links.quote: GPT-4o demonstrated a comparable level of scientific consensus to electrophysiologists, while achieving a lower error rate and significantly higher levels of specialized content, empathy, and helpfulness.

links.effect: Incorrect content: DB 29.0%, PubMed 29.0%, GPT-4o 12.1%, EP 23.0%; lifestyle consensus DB 56.7%, PubMed 60.0%, GPT-4o/EP 93.3%.
links.quote: However, the RAG models showed weaker performance than GPT-4o alone in areas requiring comprehensive understanding and reasoning.

links.effect: No/mild possible harm: DB 75.8%, PubMed 78.0%, GPT-4o 90.9%, EP 79.0%; severe/fatal possible harm: 3.0%, 2.0%, 0%, 1.0%.
links.quote: When compared with the electrophysiologist, the proportions rated as “No/mild” for Extent of Possible Harm were 75.8% for DB GPT, 78.0% for PubMed GPT, and 90.9% for GPT-4o, with no statistically significant differences observed (DB GPT: OR 0.82 [0.37–1.86]; PubMed GPT: OR 0.94 [0.41–2.14]; GPT-4o: OR 2.71 [0.98–7.51]).

As shown in Fig. 1 , for Bedside Manner (rated on a 5-point scale, 1 = very empathetic, 5 = not empathetic), GPT-4o demonstrated significantly higher empathy compared with the electrophysiologist (odds ratio = 5.55, 95% CI 2.60–11.82), whereas DB GPT (OR = 0.70, 95% CI 0.34–1.45) and PubMed GPT (OR = 0.65, 95% CI 0.31–1.36) showed comparable levels.

links.outcome: Scientific consensus and error rates of RAG versus baseline LLM
links.effect: Scientific consensus was 88.0% for GPT-4o vs 67.0% for DB GPT (OR 0.46) and 62.0% for PubMed GPT (OR 0.35) vs 80.0% for electrophysiologists; GPT-4o achieved lower error rates than RAG models.
links.quote: GPT-4o demonstrated a comparable level of scientific consensus to electrophysiologists, while achieving a lower error rate and significantly higher levels of specialized content, empathy, and helpfulness.
